records.candidate_name: Saramacca River system (southern headwaters–Coppename confluence corridor)
records.supported_name_scope: Saramacca River identifies the connected named trunk and representative system. It is not assigned uniformly to the initial small feeder or to a continuation through the shared Coppename estuary.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The actual selected southern approach, middle eastward bend, sustained northward course west of Brokopondo and westward coastal turn jointly distinguish Saramacca from the adjacent Coppename and Suriname trunks.
records.region: Central and north-central Suriname, from the interior highlands west of the upper Suriname drainage through Para to the Saramacca coastal plain.
records.completion_scope: Completed for bounded representative-system identity from original cartography covering the upper approach, middle trunk and lower river. The first feeder and exact hydronym, confluence and tidal boundary vertices remain unassigned; these limits do not prevent representative identification.

naming_scope_details.upper_scope: The actual southwestern feeder approach was inspected, not replaced with a textbook source. The first small feeder remains unnamed. Toekoemoetoe is a separately mapped western tributary, not an additional selected branch or an alias assigned to the whole route.
naming_scope_details.middle_scope: The Jan Basi Gado bend and corridor west of Brokopondo connect the selected upper and lower portions.
naming_scope_details.terminal_scope: Lower Saramacca through the coastal plain to the Coppename junction setting; excludes an asserted complete shared estuary or open-ocean continuation.
naming_scope_details.source_authority_limit: The two Naturalis-hosted maps are institutional geographic illustrations, not Suriname government naming decisions. The ministry's own water-quality map independently supports lower-river usage and sequence. No unacquired maritime chart is treated as map evidence.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: Modeled length and piece boundaries do not establish official river length or name boundaries. No formal naming date, historical alias sequence, Indigenous-name equivalence or Korean form is established. Historical cartography is used for corridor correspondence, not current settlement, infrastructure or boundary status.

records.supported_name_scope: The selected route supports the Vaza-Barris identity from the upper corridor west of Uauá, through Cocorobó and Canudos, then across Bahia and Sergipe to the lower estuarine setting. This is a representative system finding, not a name assignment to every modeled segment.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The entire selected mainstem was compared with readable official maps. Its Uauá–Cocorobó–Canudos approach, Jeremoabo bend, Bahia–Sergipe crossing and estuarine continuation distinguish it from the separate Bendengó, Itapicuru, Sergipe and Piauí corridors.
records.region: Northeastern Bahia and central/southern Sergipe, Brazil.
records.completion_scope: Completed bounded route correspondence using two readable original official maps. The extreme initial feeder/source limit, reservoir crossing channel and exact terminal estuarine channel/mouth remain unassigned; these limits do not require pending source acquisition.

naming_scope_details.system_scope: System is an editorial qualifier for the selected river group; the evidence does not name every modeled vertex or subsidiary channel.
naming_scope_details.upper_scope: Mapped western Vaza-Barris approach to Uauá; no replacement with a textbook source coordinate or a differently named tributary.
naming_scope_details.reservoir_scope: Cocorobó is a route anchor, not a replacement river name or an assignment of its entire shoreline and arms.
naming_scope_details.tributary_scope: Bendengó, Salgado, Lombada, Traíras and Tejupeba are distinct contributing context, not additional selected branches.
naming_scope_details.terminal_scope: Lower estuarine corridor; individual island channels, exact ocean mouth and tidal limit remain unspecified.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: The modeled length and fragment boundary do not establish natural-river length, hydronym boundaries, present flow permanence or current reservoir conditions.

records.supported_name_scope: West Aishihik River is supported downstream of the Bear Lakes setting; the succeeding selected reaches correspond to lower Aishihik River, Dezadeash River and Alsek River. The three tributary pieces correspond to one Tatshenshini River corridor. None of those labels is extended over the unresolved initial approach, across every lake passage, or uniformly across the seven-piece group.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The actual selection has a western northern loop toward Bear Lakes, a southeastward West Aishihik approach, the southward lower Aishihik and westward Dezadeash bends, the southbound Alsek corridor through the Lowell Lake setting, a separate eastern Tatshenshini branch, and the Alsek Lake–Dry Bay ending. The initial loop is near the mapped Twelfth of July Creek terrain and a management-subzone boundary; its apparent continuity into Bear Lakes is not established. The selected line does not follow the Sekulmun–Aishihik–Canyon lake chain or the western Kaskawulsh Glacier/River arm as its headwater route.
records.region: Southwestern Yukon, northwestern British Columbia and the Dry Bay coast of southeastern Alaska.
records.completion_scope: Completed whole-selection correspondence review and naming-scope hold using readable original map pixels. The downstream and tributary identities are recorded separately. Positive evidence of the initial modeled connection would be required before any whole-object name assignment. No further acquisition is pending for this bounded assessment.

naming_scope_details.initial_connection_hold: The first modeled loop is not assigned a river name or described as a proven feeder into Bear Lakes. Detailed source cartography shows nearby Twelfth of July Creek and an intervening boundary/terrain setting, but does not establish the complete modeled surface-water connection. This uncertainty alone prevents promoting the downstream Alsek identity to the entire selected object.
naming_scope_details.excluded_headwater_substitutions: Sekulmun Lake, its outlet river, Aishihik Lake, Canyon Lake and their outlet branch are contextual contributing waters rather than the selected northern route. The Kaskawulsh Glacier/River arm and the upstream Dezadeash Lake arm are also separate from the selected approach.
naming_scope_details.engineering_scope: The 1973 federal diagram depicts a proposed Aishihik power canal, tunnel and control works as well as natural waterways. It is used to distinguish branches, not to assert that the selected line traverses the later canal or tunnel or represents current operational flow. No power-project proposal is treated as an existing surface connection.
naming_scope_details.tributary_scope: Fragments 2747–2749 support a selected lower Tatshenshini corridor. Fragment boundaries do not delimit hydronyms, and the neighboring Takhanne, Klukshu and other side branches are not added to the group.
naming_scope_details.terminal_scope: Alsek Lake passage and Dry Bay coastal approach are supported at map scale. The NPS 2020–2021 study context is not a new observation of the 2026 glacier front, shoreline or outlet configuration; its prospective route is not substituted for the selected line.
naming_scope_details.historical_and_map_scope: The 1973 fisheries diagram and 2008/2012 Yukon sheets provide dated branch and landform context. Hunting restrictions, management boundaries, wildlife concentrations and conservation designations are not presented as current legal or ecological facts.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: The four modeled mainstem pieces and three tributary pieces do not establish one uniform river name or prove every modeled connection. Model length is not official river length. Exact first-feeder identity, transition vertices, current lake/ice boundaries, historical alias sequence, formal naming dates and a Korean form remain unassigned. No gazetteer-derived naming prose is used.

records.supported_name_scope: No natural river identity is established for the complete modeled Inland Ice path. This completed feature-class and naming-scope hold does not claim that every nearby marginal stream is unnamed.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Southeastern Greenland Inland Ice: a long southern interior route followed by an eastward bend and a southeastward approach toward the glaciated margin in the wider Tasiilaq–Sermilik–Køge Bugt region. These coastal names are regional anchors only; the exact terminal natural feature is unassigned.
records.completion_scope: Readable coverage supports the completed scope hold. Positive natural-river identity evidence would be required before any later name assignment; no further acquisition is pending now.

naming_scope_details.length_limit: Model display length, not a measured natural-river length.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Keep the saved order unchanged and use later result IDs/status changes to mark progress. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated; no lake research until all river continental phases have had their review pass.
